name: Creator Motion Graphics
look: The high-energy business-creator edit: huge condensed caps slamming in word by word, a yellow serif accent on the one word that matters, highlighter swipes, hand-drawn circles and arrows, tilted browser and phone mockups, rolling green counters, film grain and light leaks on near-black.
how: Every idea gets its own beat: words land on the beat with punch zooms and shake, the wrong idea gets a red strike and a stamp, proof appears as code-drawn mockups, the key number rolls up and locks with a boom, and whip pans, RGB glitches and flash cuts carry you between scenes.
demo: How to land your first client
replace: TL, CUTS, PUNCH, SHAKE, FLASH, LEAK, PUSH, the value curves, the scene functions, SCENES, the chrome() label text and scoreSound()
keep: slam, row, swipe, slamMarked, strike, scribble, handArrow, drawYaw, bubble, background, finishing and the compositor
sizes: keep statement text at 80 px or more, any label the story depends on at 28 px or more, and key numbers at 120 px or more
voLine: Every on-screen word slams in at the start of its spoken word, within 0.03 s. Show 2 to 6 key words per sentence, not a full transcript.
sheet: Surface: a near-black editing-room background with slow warm and cool glows, a faint drifting grid, a vignette and film grain stepped at 24 fps. Run background() and finishing() on every frame at the reference’s strength.

Type: Anton in caps for statements, set big (80 to 220 px). Instrument Serif italic in yellow for the one soft or emotional phrase. Inter for labels and small supporting lines. At most one yellow word per line; green only for money and growth numbers; red only for the wrong idea.

How things appear: words slam in one at a time (large and blurred, settling with an expo ease). Cards, chips and pills pop with overshoot. Mockups swing in with a 3D tilt (drawYaw) or slide up from below.

Emphasis: punch zoom plus shake on the hardest words; a yellow highlighter swipe that turns the word dark; a hand-drawn circle and arrow onto the thing that matters; a red strike-through for the wrong idea; a stamp for a flat rejection.
Numbers: a rolling counter in green with a glow. When it locks: a boom, a white flash, a light leak and spark streaks.

Proof shots: stylized mockups drawn in code (browser pages, phone chats, dashboards, cards) with invented, generic names. No real logos, brand names or real people, and nothing that would pass as a real receipt or a real message. Label figures as examples when they are illustrative.

Scene changes: every new idea gets a cut, rotating between whip pans with motion blur, RGB glitches and flash cuts. Inside a scene keep things continuous: lines stack, shift up, get struck out, and new lines arrive.
Chrome: a small topic label at the top left, plus a STEP pill only when the content is a real sequence.
Pace: the hook lands in under 2 seconds, something new happens every 0.5 to 1.5 seconds, and the takeaway holds about 1.5 seconds at the end.
sound: Music: a low drone and a riser into the first big word, the half-time beat (k.music) under the body, a tape stop on the wrong idea, and the beat back for the takeaway. Booms duck the music on their own.

Map events to the kit: word slams get "slam" (bigger word, more gain); pills, chips and cards get "pop"; cuts get "whoosh", "glitch" or a "slam" on the flash; highlighter and hand-drawn marks get "marker"; strike-throughs get "strike"; typing gets "keys"; a sent message "send", an incoming one "ping"; clicks "click"; counters "tick" only when the shown number changes and never more than 12 per second; the big number lands on "boom" + "slam" + "shimmer"; a rejection gets "stamp".

name: Chalk Talk
look: A teacher at a long green slate: grainy chalk strokes that skip over the board’s tooth, colored chalk for emphasis, dust falling from the stick as it writes, faint ghosts of old lessons, a wooden frame and a dusty chalk tray.
how: One continuous lesson along the board: a visible chalk stick writes every word and draws every line, the camera tracks to the next stretch of slate, numbers are re-chalked as they count, pink chalk rings the key moments, and a felt eraser wipes a section clean for the takeaway.
demo: Get 1% better every day
replace: TL, CAM, the counter curve (cntStep, cntVal, cntText), ITEMS, drawCounter(), WIPE and its timing, and scoreSound()
keep: board(), tooth(), noise2, chalkLine, chalkText, layoutText, resample, quad, ellipse, wipeMask, the frame and tray, the chalk stick, the eraser, dust() and the compositor
sizes: keep headings at 90 px or more, chalked writing at 56 px or more, labels at 36 px or more, and key numbers at 72 px or more
voLine: Each line of chalk starts being written as its first word is spoken and finishes by the end of that phrase; a short label can land on a single word. Write the key phrase on the board, not the whole transcript.
sheet: Surface: one long slate (BW wide, 720 tall) baked once with mottled green, faint chalk ghosts of old lessons and old eraser smears. The tooth pattern is punched out of the chalk layer every frame so strokes break like real chalk. Keep the wooden frame, the tray with chalk pieces, the classroom light falloff and the fine grain.

Writing: everything appears by being chalked on in order. Letters arrive one at a time with a little jitter; lines are drawn along their path with small skips. The chalk stick follows the tip whenever something is being written, and dust falls from it.

Type: Cabin Sketch for titles and the big takeaway, Kalam for equations, labels and notes. White chalk for content, yellow for the main idea and curves, pink for emphasis and key numbers, blue for side notes. Exponents and small marks use the dy offset on text parts.
Camera: one board, one continuous shot. The camera tracks along the slate to a fresh stretch for each new idea (CAM keys) and leans in gently on the key moment. No cuts.
Emphasis: pink rings around the key number or point, yellow underlines and brackets, chalk arrows that lead the eye along the board.
Numbers: re-chalked as they count (a fresh scrawl about 10 times a second), then ringed when they land.
Scene change: the felt eraser wipes a section back and forth, leaving a faint haze, and the next idea is written in the cleared space.
Diagrams: draw real charts to scale for the topic, with axes, labels and curves computed from the actual function.
Pace: something is always being written. Allow 0.4 to 1.2 seconds per line and hold the takeaway about 1.5 seconds.
sound: Bed: quiet room tone only, no music. A double knock on the board can open the lesson.

Chalk: every word gets its own scratch (grainy band-passed noise bursts with a tap where the stick lands), timed by character position across its write window. Lines get one long scratch; rings and underlines a little louder. Use the score helpers tap, scratch, write and pluck, built on k.hiss and k.voice.
Counter: a short scratch each time the shown number changes. Eraser: a felt swish for each pass, panned with the eraser.
Big moments: soft plucked notes, two for a landed number and a rising arpeggio for the takeaway. Keep it gentle; this is a lesson, not a trailer.

name: Clean Tech

how: Short statements rise word by word and the key word gets a blue pill. Ideas become small working diagrams: a prompt card that types and sends, nodes that pop in, a dot that travels a loop, task rows that tick off, a counter that climbs, a document that fills in. Clean push and zoom-through cuts move between ideas.
fonts: Inter Tight (500 to 800), JetBrains Mono (500 and 700)

keep: the ui-kit helpers (rr, track, rise, riseLine, pillBehind, typed, softCard, checkMark, composite, padBed), background(), cam() and the vignette in explainer()

sheet: Surface: cool off-white (#f5f6f8) with a slowly drifting dot grid, a faint blue glow top right and a faint green glow bottom left, and a light vignette. Keep background() and the vignette on every frame.

Type: Inter Tight 800 for statements, centered or left aligned, never all caps. Inter Tight 500 to 700 for card text. JetBrains Mono in caps with letter spacing for small labels (THE SHIFT, TASKS, STEPS TAKEN). Ink #0d0f14, muted grey for secondary text, electric blue #2f5bff as the only accent, green #18b46b only for done and checked.

How things appear: each word rises from behind a mask with an expo ease (rise, riseLine). Cards slide up and fade in, nodes pop in with a small overshoot, text in input cards is typed with a blinking caret.
Emphasis: a blue pill grows behind the one key word and the word turns white (pillBehind). Small blue glows on whatever is active. A green check pops in for anything finished.

Diagrams: build ideas from small UI pieces drawn in code: white rounded cards (softCard), mono labels, progress bars, a dashed path with a travelling dot, a counter. Use invented, generic names for any companies or products.
Camera: a gentle push-in over each scene and a small bump when a pill lands (cam with BUMPS).
Scene changes: clean horizontal pushes for a new idea and a zoom-through into a detail (composite with CUTS). No glitches or flashes.
Pace: the hook lands in under 2 seconds, one new element every 0.3 to 1 second, and the takeaway holds about 1.5 seconds.
sound: Bed: a soft synth pad (padBed) with light hats and a gentle kick under the body, dropping out for the hook and the ending.

Map events to the kit: rising words get a tiny glassy tick (rise1); blue pills get a clean swipe with a bell note; cards and nodes get "pop"; typing gets "keys" and sending gets "send"; scene pushes get "whoosh"; a zoom-through gets a short "riser" then a whoosh; finished tasks and checks get a two-note chime; counters "tick" only when the shown number changes.

name: Software Walkthrough
look: A polished screen-recording tutorial built entirely in code: an app window on a soft gradient desktop, a real-feeling cursor with click ripples, a camera that zooms into what matters, yellow-edged spotlights, numbered step callouts and a calm pad underneath.
how: It shows the clicks, not just the idea: a title card, then the cursor moves through the real flow while the camera follows it in and out, modals and menus open, fields get typed, toggles flip, and a dark step pill at the bottom left counts you through. It ends on the result actually happening and a short lower third.
fonts: DM Sans (400 to 700), DM Mono (400 and 500)
demo: Your first automation in an invented app called Flowdesk

The whole UI is drawn in code, crisp and believable, for an invented app with an invented name. Never copy a real product’s UI, name or logo.

Type: DM Sans for all UI and titles (700 for headings and selected items, 400 to 500 for body), DM Mono in caps for tiny labels (WHEN, THEN, LIVE). Ink #14161c, muted #6a6f7c, one accent (#5b5bf6) for buttons, selection and the cursor ripple, green #1fb46e for live and success, yellow #ffd60a only for spotlight edges.

Cursor: a classic arrow that moves along eased waypoints (CURSOR keys), dips slightly on each click, and leaves an accent ripple. Every click has a visible result within 0.1 s: a pressed button, a selected row, an opened menu.
Camera: one continuous screen recording. Zoom in (1.2x to 1.6x) toward the area being used, hold, and ease back out to the full window between steps (CAM keys). The camera leads the cursor slightly.
Emphasis: a spotlight dims everything except a rounded cutout with a yellow edge around the one control that matters. Toasts, notifications and a side panel slide in to prove the result.

Chrome: a title card first (small mono tag, a big two-line title, a pill with the step count and time), a dark numbered step pill at the bottom left that swaps as each step starts, and a dark lower third with a green check at the end.

Flow: real UI behaviour in order: navigate, empty state, modal with choices, dropdown, continue, editor with connected nodes, typed fields, chips, a toggle that turns on, and the outcome happening (a new row, a message, a file).
Pace: 3 to 5 seconds per step, never more than one new action at a time, and a 1.5 second hold on the result.
sound: Bed: a warm, slow pad (padBed) with soft hats while the steps run, no kick. It drops away under the title card for a moment.

Map events to the kit: every cursor click gets "click"; modals, menus, nodes and chips get "pop" (higher pitch for smaller things); typing gets "keys"; every camera zoom in or out gets a soft pink-noise swell; step pills get a two-note chime that climbs a little with each step; the toggle gets a short bright swish; a toast or the result gets a chime; an incoming notification gets "ping"; panels sliding in get a soft "whoosh".

name: Data Story
look: A calm, editorial data explainer: deep ink background, one warm accent per idea (coral, teal, sand), Archivo headlines, IBM Plex Mono numbers and labels, charts that draw themselves to scale, and the source always on screen.
how: Numbers count up, then shrink into a label as the chart arrives. A line draws itself through the real data with dots popping at each milestone, the part that matters is re-traced in sand, bars grow one by one and get ringed, two cards set the key comparison side by side, and a plain-language takeaway lands with a sand pill.
fonts: Archivo (500 to 800), IBM Plex Mono (500 and 600)

sheet: Data first: use real, sourced numbers for my topic and plot them to scale (no invented values, no cropped axes that exaggerate). Put a short "Source: ..." line at the bottom left of every frame. If a figure is an estimate, say so in the narration or a label. If you cannot verify a number, ask me instead of guessing.
Surface: deep ink (#0f141c) with a faint coral glow top left and a faint teal glow bottom right, very subtle gridlines, and a vignette.

Type: Archivo 800 for headlines and big numbers, IBM Plex Mono for every label, axis value, unit and the source line, and a small coral mono tag in caps above each headline. Ink #eef1f5, muted #7d8796.
Color has meaning: one accent per idea. Coral for the main series, teal for supporting bars, sand (#f2c14e) for the one thing the viewer should remember. Never more than three colors on screen.

Charts: lines draw left to right with a glowing head and a soft area fill, using a monotone curve through the real points so it never overshoots; milestone dots pop as the line passes them; bars grow from the baseline one by one with their value counting up on top; the key bar or span gets a sand ring or a sand re-trace with a glow.
Numbers: big counters with thousands separators count up with an expo ease and lock; a comparison card pair shows two numbers side by side with a sand multiplier counting between them.
Scene changes: soft slide-ups and clean pushes (composite with CUTS). The first number can shrink into a chart label so the opening flows into the chart without a cut.
Takeaway: one plain sentence in Archivo with a sand pill behind the key phrase, then a single mono context line. Hold about 1.5 seconds.
sound: Bed: a low, thoughtful pad (padBed) with a soft pulse once the charts start; no big drums.

Map events to the kit: counters "tick" only when the shown number changes, rising in pitch; each data milestone the line passes gets a soft pluck that climbs a pentatonic scale; each bar gets a pluck whose pitch follows its height; rings and pills get a bright swipe; scene changes get "whoosh"; cards get "pop"; the single biggest number lands on "boom" with a bell note; the takeaway gets an open chord.

name: Warm Canvas

On the canvas, a title chip lands, then one idea per beat: two cards with a dashed arrow, a comparison table whose numbers count up, a planner window where the bad blocks get flagged and removed, and three takeaway pills. Chapter cards push in vertically.

Keep the "Load A-roll" button and window.loadARoll(url) working so I can drop in my clip and see it in sync; until then the defocused stand-in shows where I sit in frame. If I give you my recording, time everything to it.

Two modes only. Mode 1: full-frame A-roll with at most one centered caption (white Fraunces 600 with a soft shadow, key words in sky blue #4f9cf0) and small white side chips with an icon and a two-line label. Mode 2: the warm canvas (#f7f5f4 with one big soft swoosh #ebe6e2), the speaker in a rounded 272x384 picture-in-picture at the right with a thin blue ring, and the content centered in the left column (COLX).

Type: Fraunces 600 for headlines, captions and card titles, tracked -2%, in two tones (ink #111111 plus sky blue for the key phrase). Inter 500 to 600 for UI labels, tags and small text in #2b2826 and #8f8a87. Title case for headlines.
Cards: white, radius 20, a very soft warm shadow, pastel tinted tags (blue, purple, green, yellow tints) and simple code-drawn icons. Never more than one window or two cards on the canvas at once.

One idea per beat: a title chip at the top of the column, then the explanation (cards with a dashed arrow, a table, a mock app window, or three takeaway pills). Each beat clears before the next arrives.

Motion is gentle: fades with a small rise (enter), soft counters, cards that slide together, never a bounce or a shake. Chapter cards (a blue number tile, a two-tone title and a progress dash row) push in and out vertically. Everything else is a clean cut.
Show me 2 to 4 beats on the canvas between A-roll moments, and come back to the full-frame A-roll for the personal lines.
sound: Quiet and tactile, built to sit under a real voice: soft paper slides (pink noise through a rising bandpass) for chips, cards and title chips, low wooden taps for list items, pills and table rows, a light keyboard patter for counters, a breathy swell for each vertical push, and one quiet pad under the canvas section.
No chimes, bells, pings, sparkles or risers, and no music beat. Never more than 2 sounds at once.

name: Pop Info
look: A flat-vector animated infographic, drawn entirely in code: a cosy cartoon scene (here a grocery aisle in soft perspective), one small character with a big feeling, a teal thought bubble that carries the idea, a counter, a dotted path and an iris wipe in and out. Muted room colours, warm product colours, rounded Fredoka type.

The idea appears as a bubble with a friendly mascot, a number counts up inside it with a little tag, a dotted path draws through the scene to a pin, and the camera slowly pushes toward the point of interest. An iris closes on the takeaway.

Invent the setting and characters for my topic; never copy a real brand, logo, mascot or packaging.
Draw in the 680 x 383 design space and let renderAt() scale it, so the art stays crisp at any size. Keep shapes big and readable on a phone.

Palette: a muted, desaturated room (sage wall #D7DCCB, warm floor #C4B79D), warm accent objects (#E07A5F, #F2CC8F, #81B29A, #6C9BB8), deep teal #2F6F73 for the idea bubble, coral #E85D4A for alerts and signs, and sunny yellow #FFD86B for tags, the iris ring and sparkles. Text is white or dark teal.

One character with a strong, simple emotion (eyebrows, mouth, blinks, a sweat drop, a sigh) is the emotional anchor. It sits in the foreground with gentle parallax while the camera pushes the background.

The idea lives in a bubble: a friendly mascot or icon, a number that counts up with an eased curve, and a small pill tag. Numbers must be real or clearly framed as an example; if you cannot verify one, ask me.

Motion is springy and playful: things pop in with a back-eased scale (popS), settle with a decaying wobble, the scene slides in from the sides, a dotted path draws itself and a pin drops, and the camera does one slow push. Open and close with the teal iris wipe with a yellow ring.
Keep it to one scene per idea, with clear staging: setting, character reaction, the idea in the bubble, the visual proof (path, arrow or chart), then the iris closes.
sound: Soft, toy-like and sparse: rounded pops for the bubble, tags and pin, little sine bloops for character reactions, wooden taps for landings, counter steps and path dots (thinning out as the counter lands), airy whooshes for the iris and the slides, and one breathy sigh.
No chimes, bells, pings or sparkle sounds, even for winks and sparkles on screen. The cartoon carries the charm; the sound only gives it weight.

Each beat gets one rounded card with a big word, a gauge or a counter, and the camera pulls back for the takeaway.

sound: Bed: a bright, simple pad (padBed) with light hats, and a soft kick only during the action.

name: Marker Board

name: Blueprint

Dimension lines with arrowheads and mono measurements; callouts in JetBrains Mono on thin leader lines; a title block in the bottom-right corner with sheet number and scale.

Pace: ink-in about 2 seconds, then the mechanism in 2 to 3 seconds, the success beat, the failure beat, and the takeaway.
sound: Bed: a soft, steady pad with a slow pulse.

Map events to the kit: line work gets drafting-pen scratches (SND.scratch); each part that lifts or drops gets a small metallic click; success gets a two-note chime and "click"; failure gets a dull thud; the takeaway gets an open chord.

Ransom-note titles: each letter in its own box with a random font (Anton, Playfair Display, Special Elite, Archivo Black, Bangers), colour pair and small rotation, all seeded so it never changes between frames.

Characters are simple and expressive: round heads, big white eyes with dots, eyebrows and an open mouth, a sweat drop for stress. Original characters only, never a known comic hero.
Speech balloons are white ellipses with a black outline and a pointed tail; captions are yellow boxes; sound effects are spiky bursts with Bangers lettering in yellow with a thick black stroke.
Camera: zoom into one panel at a time in reading order (CAMK), eased; shake on the big sound effect; pull out to the full page at the end.

name: Parchment Map
look: An aged ink map on stained parchment: hand-inked coastlines with a second faint outline, a graticule, burnt edges, a compass rose, a little sailing ship and a red dashed route that draws itself as the camera follows it across the map.

Project lon/lat to the map with one scale; route waypoints carry their real coordinates and their arrival time, so the ship always moves at story speed.
The route is a red (#a3261c) dashed line that grows behind the ship, with an arrowhead at the front. The ship is a small inked hull with two sails that bobs on the waves.
The camera pans across the map following the ship; the title and stamps stay fixed on screen.
Type: Playfair Display 900 for the title (second line italic), Special Elite typewriter text for date stamps on cream labels with a red border.
Burnt edges (a dark brown vignette) and paper grain on top of everything.

sound: Bed: a slow, low sea swell (brown noise with a slow filter sweep) and a warm, sparse pad.

Map events to the kit: the drawing route gets a soft quill scratch (SND.scratch); each stamp gets a stamp thud ("stamp" at low gain) and a soft bell; storms or deaths get a low swell; the takeaway gets an open chord.

name: Timeline Rail

fonts: Archivo Black, Space Grotesk (700), Inter (600 and 700)
demo: The phone in 150 years
replace: TL, EVENTS (year, text, icon painter), the scroll keys, the headline, the takeaway and scoreSound()
keep: the long content layer with the rail, nodes and cards, the scroll camera, the drop-in card motion, the year odometer, the icon painter approach (small flat icons in the page colour), wordLine() and grain()

sheet: One long vertical page (a content layer taller than the screen) in deep green (#0f2a24) with a cream rail (#e8dcc0) down the left. The camera scrolls down it; no cuts.
Each event is a cream card (#f3ead7) with rounded corners, a big gold year (#e8b04b) in Space Grotesk, one short line of text and a small flat icon drawn in code in the page colour.
The current node glows gold; past nodes stay filled, future nodes stay hollow.
A year odometer in the top-right rolls between events (digits slide), always showing the year the camera is at.
Use real dates and real firsts; keep each card to one line of fact.
Pace: about 2 seconds per card, including the scroll.
sound: Bed: a warm pad with a soft clock-like pulse.
Map events to the kit: each scroll gets a soft "whoosh"; the odometer gets fast ticks while it rolls; each card gets a soft thud as it lands and a chime; the takeaway gets an open chord.

name: Isotype
look: Pictogram statistics in the Isotype tradition: a grid of small grey people icons that pop in row by row, then the share that matters turns coral one by one and regroups into its own block, under one huge number.

fonts: Archivo Black, Inter (500 and 800), JetBrains Mono (700)
demo: 1 in 3 US adults sleep less than 7 hours
replace: TL, the stat (RATIO, the headline text and the big number), the icon shape in personIcon() if the subject is not people, the source line, the takeaway and scoreSound()

Icons are simple and identical: a round head and a rounded body, grey (#c3ced8) by default, coral (#ff5a3c) for the share that matters. No other colours.
Background: cool pale grey-blue (#edf2f6); text in deep navy (#13212e).
Order: fill the crowd row by row, colour the share one by one, then move the coloured icons into a solid block at the start of the grid (sorted target slots) so the split reads at a glance.
Type: Archivo Black for the big number, Inter 800 for the statement (second line in coral), JetBrains Mono for the source line at the bottom.
Pace: crowd in about 1.5 seconds, colour fill about 2 seconds, regroup about 1.5 seconds.
sound: Bed: a calm, light pad (padBed).
Map events to the kit: each row gets a soft "tick"; each coloured icon gets a short pluck that climbs; the big number gets "slam"; the regroup gets a soft "whoosh"; the takeaway gets an open chord.

name: Evidence Board

Clues are physical objects drawn in code: polaroids (white frame, dark photo area with a simple sketch, Caveat caption), lined index cards with Special Elite typing, yellow sticky notes in Caveat, each slightly rotated with a drop shadow and a red pin.
Red string (#c1121f) sags between pins and draws itself from one pin to the next.
Verdict: a rubber stamp (red, double border, distressed with knocked-out specks) slams onto the board with a shake.

sound: Bed: a low, tense pad and a slow pulse.

Map events to the kit: pins get a soft push (SND.tap low); string gets a short twang (a plucked low note with a bend); typing gets "keys"; camera moves get a soft "whoosh"; the stamp gets "stamp" and a low "boom".

keep: the paper grain, wash() bloom (layered irregular blobs with soft edges), inkPath() line reveal, the gold ink stars, the word-by-word storyline, the page frame and the page-turn cut

Washes: each area is several overlapping irregular blobs at low alpha (wash()), blooming outward from a centre over about a second, with a slightly darker edge.
Ink: one thin brown line (#3a2a20, 2 to 3 px) that draws the character and key objects along their path. Small gold details (#e8c35a) for stars and sparkles.
Palette: night blue washes (#2d4a8a), warm moon (#f6e1a0), green hills (#6a9a5b), the character in one warm colour (#e0793a).

Map events to the kit: each wash gets a soft brush swish (SND.paper, soft); ink lines get a very quiet scratch; stars get small high chimes; page turns get a longer paper sweep; the ending gets a gentle chord.

keep: the black screen with phosphor glow, the line-by-line session renderer with typed commands and printed output, the block cursor, the ASCII progress bar, scanlines and vignette, and the colour rules

Map events to the kit: typed commands get "keys"; each printed line gets a soft short beep (SND.beep); a bad result gets a two-tone alarm; a good result gets a rising confirm beep; the takeaway gets a low swell.

name: Math Canvas

demo: Compound interest: slow, then suddenly fast
replace: TL, the equation pieces (EQ), the function f(x) and the comparison g(x), the axis ranges and ticks, the labels, the gap note, the takeaway and scoreSound()

name: Glitch Pack

Slices: copy horizontal bands of the canvas onto itself shifted left or right; block noise: small red, cyan and white rectangles.
Scanlines every 3 px and a dark vignette on top; a small mono tag ("> SYSTEM REBOOT", "v2.0") in a corner.
Respect photosensitivity: no full-frame white flashes faster than 3 a second.

Map events to the kit: glitch moments get "glitch" plus bit-crushed square zaps; the title resolve gets "slam" and a low sub drop (a falling sine); transitions get "whoosh" with a "glitch"; tags get small beeps.

name: Doc Cinema

name: VHS Camcorder

Map events to the kit: REC, PLAY and REW get a mechanical "click"; the rewind gets a fast warbling, pitch-rising noise; the tracking band gets a short crackle burst.
